Jordan / Rachel — attaching the initial evidence packet for the encryption section and a recent rotation audit extract. Highlights below; details are in the attached PDF/CSV.

- In-transit: All network communications to hosted APIs use TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 is supported and negotiated when the client supports it. We publish cipher suites in the evidence PDF.
- At-rest: Customer and model data volumes are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. Data keys (DEKs) are envelope-encrypted with a per-tenant KEK.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood uses HSM-backed KMS for root key material. For our public hosted offering we use Redwood-managed keys by default (AWS KMS + CloudHSM FIPS 140-2 Level 3 for root), and we offer BYOK where customers can provide or escrow keys in their own KMS (supported: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- Custody & attestation: We can provide CloudHSM attestation statements and our recent HSM inventory snapshot. Some customers with stricter requirements opt for Private deployments with customer-controlled HSMs — that is supported and documented.
- Rotation cadence: DEKs are rotated automatically on a rolling schedule (default 7–30 days depending on workload), KEKs (tenant-level) are rotated every 90 days by default; root keys are rotated annually and require HSM-backed ceremonies.
- Audit logs: Rotation events and KMS operations are logged; sample export included (kms-rotation-audit-2027-07.csv).

Attachments: redwood-sig-encryption-evidence-v2.pdf; kms-rotation-audit-2027-07.csv

Let me know if you need signed attestation copies or specific HSM vendor reports — we can scope that.

Mina Haddad

Jordan — adding a few technical specifics to complement Mina's note, and pasting a short FAQ you can include in the SIG answers: 

1) Envelope encryption model: DEKs are generated per object/tenant and encrypted with a tenant KEK. KEKs are themselves wrapped by a root key stored in an HSM. We do not persist raw DEKs unencrypted.

2) HSM provider and attestation: For Redwood-managed keys the root key lives in AWS CloudHSM clusters (FIPS 140-2 level 3) with attestation reports available upon NDA where required. For Private/VPC deployments, customers may bring their own HSM or use their cloud provider's HSM; we document allowed topologies in the Private deployment guide.

3) Rotation mechanics: Automated rotation uses a staged rewrap: new KEK is generated, new DEKs are re-encrypted in the background, stale KEKs are retired after a grace window. Rotation logs include operation timestamps, actor (service principal), and operation type; sample fields shown in the CSV.

4) Key compromise playbook: We maintain a documented incident flow — revoke affected KEKs, rewrap DEKs to new KEK, notify customers per SLA. We can include a redacted runbook excerpt in the evidence bundle.

5) TLS specifics: Server endpoints support TLS 1.2 and 1.3. We enforce HSTS and strong ciphers; mutual TLS is available for dedicated/private endpoints on request.

If you want a short plain-English paragraph for the SIG: "Redwood encrypts data in transit using TLS (1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred) and at rest with AES-256 envelope encryption. Root key material is protected in HSMs; rotation is automated for DEKs and KEKs with an annual root key rotation practice; detailed logs and attestation reports are available for review."

Happy to provide any snippets you need to paste into the SIG.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
